title: Generation of effector Vγ9Vδ2 T cells and evaluation of their response to phosphoantigen-loaded cells
protocol: Thaw PBMCs quickly by hand or in water bath.
Wash thawed cells once with media to remove cryoprotectant.
Centrifuge the washed cells for 3 minutes at 600 rcf at room temperature.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in 10 mL of fresh T cell media.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a vented T75 flask.
Count the cells and dilute them to a concentration of 2–4 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add IL-2 to a final concentration of 5 ng/mL using a 1:100 dilution from the working IL-2 stock.
Add HMBPP to a final concentration of 100 nM.
Grow cells in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Wash cells after 3 days to remove HMBPP.
Transfer washed cells to a 15 mL or 50 mL conical tube depending on the culture volume.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate media using vacuum suction.
Add 10 mL of fresh T cell media without disturbing the pellet.
Centrifuge again for 3 minutes at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Resuspend the cell pellet in the initial volume of fresh T cell media.
Add fresh IL-2 to a final concentration of 5 ng/mL.
Transfer all cells to a new vented T75 flask.
At day 6 and 9 post stimulation, add fresh IL-2 to 5 ng/mL.
Inspect cells at days 6 and 9 for defined colonies of 10–1000 cells.
On day 12, cells are ready for purification.
Collect all HMBPP expanded cells.
Transfer cells to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge 3 min at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate media using vacuum suction.
Resuspend in 80 μL of cold MACS buffer.
Add 20 μL biotin-antibody cocktail from TCR γ/δ+ T Cell Iso Kit, human.
Mix by gentle flicking.
Incubate for 15 min at 4°C.
Wash cells.
Add 900 μL of cold MACS buffer.
Centrifuge 3 min at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Resuspend in 80 μL MACS buffer.
Add 20 μL magnetic beads.
Incubate again for 15 min at 4°C.
Wash cells.
Add 900 μL of MACS buffer.
Centrifuge 3 min at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Resuspend in 500 μL MACS buffer.
Equilibrate the magnetic column with 500 μL of cold MACS buffer.
Pass 500 μL of cells through the magnetic column.
Elute cells 2 additional times with 500 μL cold MACS buffer.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging for 3 minutes at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Resuspend in 10 mL T cell media.
Count the cells.
Assess purity by flow cytometry staining with CD3 and γδ TCR antibodies if desired.
Maintain cells in the incubator or use them immediately after purification.
Alternatively, freeze the cells in liquid nitrogen following the freezing procedure for PBMCs.
Store typically 3 × 10^6 effector cells per 500 μL cryotube for future use.
Dilute C-HMBPP in water to prepare a stock solution.
Prepare 10-fold serial dilutions of C-HMBPP using T cell media, ranging from 1 × 10−3 to 1 × 10−7 M.
Dilute zoledronate in water to prepare a stock solution.
Prepare 10-fold serial dilutions of zoledronate using T cell media, ranging from 1 × 10−2 to 1 × 10−6 M.
Count K562 cells.
Transfer 1.2 × 10^6 cells to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate media by vacuum suction.
Resuspend K562 cells in T cell media to reach a concentration of 2 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Add 6 mL of T cell media to resuspended cells and mix by gentle pipetting.
Aliquot 120 μL of the cell suspension into sterile 200 μL strip tubes.
For each dose response, prepare six tubes with cells.
Using a multichannel pipettor, add 13.3 μL of test compound or solvent control to each tube.
Mix gently after adding the test compound or solvent.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Proceed to count and plate T cells as described in the next section during incubation.
Incubate treated K562 cells.
Wash cells 3–5 times with 120 μL of T cell media.
Centrifuge strip tubes for 20 seconds at maximum speed using a tabletop mini centrifuge.
Aspirate approximately 95% of the medium, leaving a visible small cell pellet undisturbed.
Add 120 μL of T cell media to the cells.
Repeat washing steps with 3–5 washes in total.
Resuspend cells in 120 μL of T cell media using a multichannel pipettor and proceed to co-culture.
Label a 96 well plate.
Count expanded Vγ9Vδ2 T cells.
Collect 1.2 × 10^6 T cells per plate.
Transfer collected cells to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells for 3 minutes at 600 rcf at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate the medium using vacuum suction.
Resuspend cells in T cell media to achieve a concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Add 12 mL of T cell media to reach a final cell concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells/mL (containing 1.2 × 10^6 cells).
Gently resuspend the cells by pipetting.
Add 60 μL of fresh T cell media without cells to each well of a 96 well plate using a multichannel pipettor.
For a media control, add 200 μL of media in duplicate wells.
Distribute 120 μL of T cells to each well using a multichannel pipettor.
This results in 12,000 T cells per well.
We routinely distribute 80 μL of media and 120 μL of T cells to duplicate wells as a T cell only control.
If loaded K562 cells are not ready to be added onto the plate, keep the plate at 37°C until ready.
Add 20 μL of loaded K562 cells to each well using a multichannel pipettor.
This results in 4,000 K562 cells per well.
We routinely distribute 180 μL of media and 20 μL of loaded K562 cells to duplicate wells as a K562 cell only control.
Incubate the cells for 20 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Coat ELISA plates one day prior to the ELISA experiments.
Dilute capture antibody 1:200 in 1× coating buffer.
Use a multichannel pipettor to coat ELISA plate with 100 μL/well of diluted capture antibody overnight.
Add additional 16 wells for standard curve and 6 wells for controls (media only, T cells only, and K562 cells only).
Seal the coated plate with a plate sealer and place in refrigerator.
Peel off the plate sealer the next day.
Shake out the liquid into the sink in one quick motion the following day.
Wash the ELISA plates 4 times with Wash Buffer (PBS + 0.05% Tween 20).
Fill each well to a consistent level and shake the buffer into the sink during washing.
Wash ELISA plate wells using a spray bottle method.
Cut the tip of the nozzle off the spray bottle for faster washing.
Apply similar volume and flow rate to the wash steps for each well.
Pat the plate dry on a layer of paper towels after the last wash.
Dilute assay diluent to 1× with PBS.
Prepare 40 mL of diluted assay diluent per plate.
Block plates with 200 μL of diluted assay diluent.
Seal the plate and incubate for 1 h at room temperature on a rocker.
Wash plates 4 times and dry as specified.
Prepare eight 2-fold serial dilutions of the top standard from kit.
Make the top concentration 4-fold higher than recommended in the protocol.
Transfer 25 μL of media from the assay plate to ELISA plate, avoiding bottom contact.
Incubate sealed plate for 2 h at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Wash 4 times and dry as above.
Dilute detection antibody 1:200 in 1× assay diluent, preparing 10 mL total per plate.
Add 100 μL/well of detection antibody.
Incubate sealed plate for 1 h at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Wash 4 times and dry as above.
Dilute avidin-HRP 1:1000 in 10 mL of 1× assay diluent.
Add 100 μL/well of avidin-HRP.
Incubate sealed plate for 30 min at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Wash 5 times and dry as above.
Mix TMB A and TMB B equally to form active TMB substrate solution, 10 mL total per plate.
Add 100 μL/well of detection reagent (TMB substrate solution).
Incubate 7–10 min in dark.
Add 100 μL/well of stop solution when ready.
Add stop solution to the reaction mixture as soon as possible after color development is observed.
Read absorbance at 450 nm.
Read absorbance at 550 nm for background correction.
